ESP32 Modular Base v2.0: assembly guide

Hand assembly · rev 2.0 · 2026-10
Board75 × 65 mm, 2 layers, 1.6 mm
Parts to solder68 per board
Left empty38 option footprints
Batch5 boards (tick columns B1–B5)

How to use this guide

  1. Work through the steps in order. Each step is one page: a board drawing with only that step's parts in colour, and a table.
  2. Do one step on all 5 boards before moving to the next. Tick the box for each board (B1–B5) as you finish a line.
  3. Number the boards on the back with a marker so the ticks and test results stay with the right board.
  4. Colours in a step = values. Black dots mark pin 1 (1), cathode (K) or plus (+).
  5. Footprints drawn dashed stay empty. They are options for configuring ports later.
  6. Grid squares (A–H, 1–7) help find a part: the parts index on the last page lists every reference.

Before you start

Tools · temperatures · symbols

Tools

Soldering ironTemperature controlled. Chisel or hoof tip 1.6–2.4 mm for drag soldering, a fine conical tip for 0805, a big chisel for the regulator tab and THT ground pins.
Solder0.5–0.8 mm wire with flux core. Leaded 63/37 is easiest; lead-free SAC305 needs about 30 °C more.
FluxNo-clean flux pen or gel. Use plenty on the CH340C, USBLC6 and the module.
Desoldering wick1.5–2 mm, for bridges.
TweezersFine straight or curved, non-magnetic if possible.
Magnification10× loupe or a USB microscope for checking IC pins and the module.
CleaningIsopropyl alcohol (99 %) and an old toothbrush.
MultimeterContinuity, diode test, DC volts.
OtherKapton tape, side cutters, a USB-A to C cable, a PC with a USB port.

Iron temperature (guide)

0805, SOT-23320–340 °C leaded · 350–370 °C lead-free
SOIC, module330–360 °C leaded · 360–380 °C lead-free
U2 tab, F1, THT GND pins360–390 °C with a large tip, hold longer

Prepare the boards

  1. Check each bare PCB: no scratches across tracks, holes clear, edges clean.
  2. Number the boards 1–5 on the back (marker, near a corner).
  3. Continuity check on one bare board: +5V to GND and +3V3 to GND must be open (no beep). Probe +5V on the C1 square pad, +3V3 on the C4 square pad, GND on any port pin G.
  4. Sort the parts by step. Keep each value in its own labelled bag; unmarked 0805 capacitors look identical.
  5. Work on an ESD mat or touch a grounded object before handling the CH340C, USBLC6 and the module.

Symbols on the drawings

Good joint, bad joint

  • Good: shiny (leaded) or satin (lead-free), concave fillet from pad to part, pad fully wetted.
  • Cold: grey, lumpy, ball sitting on the pad. Reheat with flux.
  • Bridge: solder joining two pins. Flux + drag, or wick.
  • Tombstone: 0805 standing on one end. Reheat the high end and press down.

Step 1: Fine-pitch ICs

2 parts per board · 10 for 5 boards

Solder these first, while the board is flat and nothing is in the way of the iron.

QtyValueReferencesPackageGridOrientation / noteB1B2B3B4B5
1CH340CU3SOIC-16F2Pin-1 dot/notch on the ●1 marker (top-left)
1USBLC6-2SC6U4SOT-23-6F2Pin-1 dot on the ●1 marker
Iron: 330–350 °C leaded, 360–380 °C lead-free
  • Flux the pads. Tin one corner pad only.
  • Place the IC with tweezers, pin 1 on the ●1 marker. Reheat the tinned pad so the pin sinks in.
  • Check alignment on all sides with a loupe. If it is off, reheat and nudge; then tack the opposite corner.
  • Drag-solder each row: plenty of flux, a little solder on a chisel or hoof tip, pull slowly along the pins.
  • Bridges: add flux and drag again, or lift with wick. Check every gap against light.

Step 2: Transistors and 3.3 V regulator

4 parts per board · 20 for 5 boards

SOT-23 and SOT-223 only fit one way round, but they are small and easy to lose: do them before the 0805 parts crowd the area.

QtyValueReferencesPackageGridOrientation / noteB1B2B3B4B5
1MMBT3904Q1SOT-23F3Fits one way (3 pads)
1MMBT3904Q2SOT-23F3Fits one way (3 pads)
1AO3400AQ901SOT-23G5Fits one way (3 pads)
1AMS1117-3.3U2SOT-223D5Big tab = right side
Iron: SOT-23: 330–350 °C. U2 tab: 360–390 °C, larger tip
  • Tin one pad, place the part, reheat to fix it, then solder the other pads.
  • AMS1117 (U2): the big tab sits on a copper heat spreader. Use a larger tip and more heat, hold 3–5 s until the solder flows over the whole tab.
  • Q1/Q2 are MMBT3904 (marking 1AM). Q901 is AO3400A (marking A09T). Do not mix them up.

Step 4: Port parts fitted by default

27 parts per board · 135 for 5 boards

Every port gets its 330 R (A series), 1 k (B series) and 0.5 A PTC. UART and I2C have their own default values. All other port footprints stay empty (dashed on the diagram) until you configure the port.

Iron: 320–340 °C leaded
  • Colour = value. Do one colour at a time across all boards.
  • UART: R704 is 10 k (not 1 k) and R706 is 22 k: together they divide 5 V down for RX.
  • I2C: R801 and R804 are 100 R, R802 and R805 are 4.7 k pull-ups.
  • PTCs (1206) have no polarity. They need a little more heat than 0805.
  • Do not fill the dashed footprints now.

Step 5: Diodes, LEDs and input PTC

5 parts per board · 25 for 5 boards

Polarised parts: check every one against the K marker before soldering the second pad.

QtyValueReferencesPackageGridOrientation / noteB1B2B3B4B5
1SMAJ5.0AD1SMAE4Band on K (toward +5V)
1SS34D901SMAG5Band on K (toward V+)
1PTC 1.1 A holdF11812E4No polarity
1LED redLED10805 LEDD4Cathode on K
1LED yellowLED20805 LEDE3Cathode on K
Iron: 340–360 °C, larger tip for F1, D1, D901
  • D1 SMAJ5.0A and D901 SS34: the band on the body is the cathode and goes on the K marker.
  • LEDs: the cathode is marked by a green dot/line on top or the bar of the T on the underside. Not sure? Multimeter in diode mode, red probe on the anode: the LED glows.
  • LED1 is red (power), LED2 is yellow (status). Do not use blue, green or white here.
  • F1 (1812) has a lot of copper: use the bigger tip and give it time.

Step 6: ESP-32S module

1 parts per board · 5 for 5 boards

The module covers nothing else, but once it is on, the area under it is closed. All SMD parts around it are done by now.

QtyValueReferencesPackageGridOrientation / noteB1B2B3B4B5
1ESP-32S (Ai-Thinker)U1ModuleD1Antenna over top edge, pin 1 top-left
Iron: 340–360 °C, chisel tip
  • Antenna end overhangs the top edge of the board. Pin 1 is top-left (●1).
  • Tin pad 1 only. Place the module, align all 38 castellations with the pads, reheat pad 1.
  • Check alignment on the left, right and bottom rows. Tack pad 38 (top-right), check again.
  • Drag-solder each side with flux. The pads are extended 1 mm so the iron reaches them.
  • Optional: feed solder into the 1 mm hole in the centre GND pad from the back.

Iron: 340–360 °C, larger tip for the ground pins

  - {platform: gpio, name: "P4 A", pin: GPIO13}
  - {platform: gpio, name: "P5 A", pin: GPIO4}
  - {platform: gpio, name: "P6 A", pin: GPIO18}
  - {platform: gpio, name: "UART TX", pin: GPIO17}
  - {platform: gpio, name: "OUT", pin: GPIO23}

Notes

  • Flash over USB: esphome run modbase-test.yaml and pick the CH340 port.
  • ESPHome warns that GPIO0 and GPIO2 are strapping pins: expected, they are the BOOT button and status LED.
  • The A pins are measured at the connector, through the 330 R: with nothing connected you read the full 3.3 V.
  • B pins are inputs; test them when you configure a port (NTC, pulse, divider).
  • IO36/IO39 (P1/P2 B) cannot drive anything: they are input-only.
  • When the board passes, flash your real configuration over USB or OTA.
  • Mains: this board is low voltage only. Keep relay modules and meters behind the divider in the box, and flash with mains disconnected.

VP and OUT jumpers

Changing a port between 3V3 and 5V

Each port's supply pin VP comes from a three-pad solder jumper. The pad nearest the connector is 3V3, the far pad is 5V, the middle pad is VP. The board ships with a thin copper trace joining the default pair: 3V3 on P1–P6 and I2C, 5V on UART.

Changing a port to 5V

  1. Power off. Find the jumper (table below), between the connector and the PTC.
  2. Cut the trace between the 3V3 pad and the middle pad with a sharp hobby knife: two or three light strokes, across the gap only.
  3. Check with the multimeter: no continuity between the two pads.
  4. Add flux and bridge the middle pad to the 5V pad with a blob of solder.
  5. Check: VP pin of the connector reads 5 V after power-up. Write the change in the table.
  6. To go back: remove the blob with wick, bridge the 3V3 side with solder instead (the trace is gone).

Only switch a port to 5V for a device that needs it, and only if the device's signal into the ESP32 stays at 3.3 V (or the port has the 10 k / 22 k divider on B). The ESP32 pins are not 5 V tolerant.

PortJumperDefaultGridChanged toDate
P1JP1013V3A6
P2JP2013V3C6
P3JP3013V3D6
P4JP4013V3F6
P5JP5013V3B2
P6JP6013V3B4
UARTJP7015VG3
I2CJP8013V3G4

JP901: OUT supply

JP901 is a two-pad jumper next to the OUT connector, open as made. Bridge it only to power a 5 V load from the board (pin V+ then carries +5V). Never bridge it while an external 12/24 V supply is on V+: that would feed 12/24 V into the board's 5 V rail.
